purpose.description: Define observation boundaries for evaluating latent-state identifiability.
purpose.role: Measure which hidden-state distinctions remain accessible through different interfaces.
purpose.principle: An interface is sufficient only if it preserves distinctions required by the target.

factorization_condition.statement: exists L_hat such that L=L_hat o O

interfaces.name: Instantaneous Observable State
interfaces.description: Observer receives only the visible component.

equivalence_structure.meaning: All states with identical x_t values collapse together.

interfaces.name: Temporal Observation Window
interfaces.description: Observer receives a sequence of past visible observations.

latent_recovery_mechanism.description: Hidden state may leave a recoverable signature through future observations.

interfaces.name: Complete Latent State Observation
interfaces.description: Observer receives both visible and hidden state variables.

interfaces.name: Active Causal Probe
interfaces.description: Observer can perturb the system and observe response changes.

latent_recovery_mechanism.description: Different hidden states produce different responses under controlled inputs.

interface_comparison.finding: Temporal and intervention interfaces can recover information unavailable from instantaneous observation.

minimality.search_objective: Find lowest-cost interface preserving target identifiability.

decision.meaning: Interfaces define the observation boundaries for hidden-state identifiability experiments.

notes: Hidden does not imply unknowable; identifiability depends on available causal pathways.
History converts static observation into dynamic observation.
Intervention adds information unavailable from passive observation.
